title: Effects of trimodal prehabilitation on well-being and complications after transcervical pharyngeal/laryngeal cancer resections.
summary:
The aim of this study is to see whether patients with extensive tumors of the pharynx and larynx can be helped with holistic preparation before a necessary major operation. 
This type of holistic preparation for surgery (“prehabilitation”) involves improving nutrition (through medical, high-calorie nutritional drinks), training the body and lungs (through breathing training, strengthening and mobilization exercises) and psychological support. 
All patients who are scheduled to undergo major surgery to remove pharyngeal/throat cancer at our Head and Neck Tumor Center can take part in this study. 
The aim is to see whether prehabilitation is feasible for patients and if/how exactly it helps them.
After the operation, the healing process is evaluated and a survey is conducted to assess satisfaction with the prehabilitation measures. 
In order to compare whether the time after the operation is more favorable for patients with prehabilitation than for patients without prehabilitation, a comparison is made with patients who have already been operated on in a similar way for similar tumor diseases (there was no prehabilitation in the past).

interventions.name: Prospectively selected patients with advanced pharyngeal/laryngeal carcinoma and indication for transcervical resection of this carcinoma according to the tumor board decision.
Retrospectively matched controls (from the pool of patients already operated on in our clinic in previous years).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with histologically confirmed, advanced pharyngeal/laryngeal carcinoma. 
- According to the tumor board decision, transcervical surgical resection via laryngectomy or pharyngotomy with flap plasty is indicated.
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Patients who are unable to give consent
- Women of childbearing age
- Patients with derailed / difficult to control diabetes mellitus (“carbohydrate loading” not possible)
- Patients with severe, uncontrolled COPD (breathing training not possible)
- Patients with intolerances to Fortimel®, preOP® or their ingredients
